question: How much does the America the Beautiful annual pass for US national parks cost for non-US residents in 2026?
answer:
The America the Beautiful annual pass costs non-US residents $250 in 2026, compared with $80 for US residents. [1][2][7] The higher nonresident price took effect January 1, 2026, when the pass was split into resident and nonresident versions. [1][7]

The $250 pass also covers the separate $100-per-person nonresident fee (for visitors 16 and older) charged at 11 heavily visited parks, including Yellowstone, Yosemite, Grand Canyon, Zion and Glacier. [2][7] A source dated Nov 1, 2026 says it covers the holder and passengers in one private car, or the holder plus three adults where fees are per person. [2] The pass covers entrance fees only, not camping, timed-entry reservations or shuttle tickets. [1]

keyPoints.text: The America the Beautiful annual pass costs $250 for nonresidents in 2026.
The resident annual pass costs $80 in 2026, so the nonresident price is more than three times higher.
The $250 nonresident pass covers the $100 per-person nonresident fee at 11 named parks for the holder and passengers in a private vehicle.
The nonresident pricing tier took effect January 1, 2026.

conflicts.text: Source 2 says the $250 pass covers the holder plus passengers in one private car, or the holder plus three adults where fees are per person, while Source 5 describes it as covering the surcharge for the pass holder without specifying passenger limits.

Source 6 (dated 2025-04-18) gives the $80 pass price, predating the 2026 nonresident tier.
